text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- CSN SEEKS PARTNERS TO COMPETE IN CVRD AUCTION

A consortium led by Brazilian steelmaker Companhia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN) is seeking new partners to compete in the April 29 auction of mining giant Vale do Rio Doce. Gazeta Mercantil said CSN chairman Benjamin Steinbruch is in talks with Garantia Participacoes, the Suzano group, the Soros Fund, Japanese trading firm Mitsubishi and Brazilian construction firm Camargo Correa.
-- MORGAN STANLEY SAYS IBOVESPA COULD RISE ANOTHER 20 PCT
The Bovespa Index could rise a further 20 percent over and beyond the 24 percent increase it has posted in dollar terms so far this year, Morgan Stanley economist Robert Pelosky said.
-- CONGRESSIONAL INVESTIGATORS TO PROBE CONSTRUCTION FIRMS
A Senate investigating committee will begin to probe construction firms and suppliers that received payments from states and municipalities which launched bond issues to finance debt roll-overs.
-- JUDGE ISSUES HEAVY SENTENCE IN SAO PAULO KILLING
A judge sentenced four men to between 23 and 48 years in prison for the 1996 murder of two young people the traditional late-night Sao Paulo Bodega bar.
-- SENATE COMMITTEE TO ACCUSE BANCO VECTOR

A Senate investigating committee will seek charges against Banco Vector, which is being accused of masterminding a multi-million dollar bond scam, on grounds that its owners conspired to commit fraud.
-- NEO-LIBERAL CHARGES COME FROM NEO-DUMMIES, SAYS CARDOSO

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said critics who accuse his administration of selling out to the "Neo-Liberals" and cutting back of social programs were "Neo-Dummies". "They have nothing in their heads those that say the government is only worried about the market, that it is Neo-Liberal. They are Neo-Dummies," Cardoso said during a speech on Monday.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
